accuracy.claim: Errors reach the caller as exceptions: domain errors (sentence plus details), one top-level handler printing FATAL on stderr and exiting 1, a FailureExit marker that only exits, and matching by sentence.

Not flagged by the baseline, from reading only: cli.ts's execWithErrorHandler throws FailureExit inside a detached .catch and returns the original promise, so for the template error the original error still reaches handleError (printed twice) and the marker is never seen. The marker works as described when InitCommand throws it.

coverage.note: R-1 b2/b4/b5 cover the options and the Slug/Status/Package/Title table; R-3 b1 the comma-separated --statuses; R-2 the raw comma-joined lines.

AD-20: the CLI is a thin adapter over the facade and calls searchAdrs, with the rules in core (the Conventions and Interfaces bullets also say data comes only from the facade). AD-12: Explicit Architecture and DDD.
R-5 b3: the slug is the file name without .md, package-prefixed, with no number and no separate id. AD-6 (accepted) replaces AD-4 (superseded). R-7 b4: no id field.
R-7 b2 lists all 13 DTO fields plus the optional repository; R-7 b4 says there is no id or date field and that three dates exist.
AD-2; the Stack bullet gives Yarn workspaces with Lerna 5 and six packages at 1.1.0; the Structure section names cli, cli-common, global-cli, core, init and web.
AD-3: Prettier-ESLint Airbnb. AD-5: no default exports, with Next.js pages and API routes exempt. Conventions bullets 1-2 add the observed style.

Each tracked record maps to exactly one AD: 11 in docs/adr (AD-4 and AD-10 are the 2 superseded ones, under Superseded), 3 in core, 5 in web. A Conventions bullet excludes the integration-test fixtures and the init/assets starter ADRs. EXPECTED's counts are wrong: git ls-files at 17e3202 shows 11 records in docs/adr (not 10) and 5 in packages/web/docs/adr (not 3), 19 in all. The baseline's 19 is right.

R-9 b6: 'The debug helper writes to standard output ... the listing path never calls it' (internal function and code path)

leakage.note: Bullets that mention a mechanism only on the way to a caller-visible result were not counted (R-9 b1 top-level handler, R-9 b8 launcher, R-1 b10 argument parser). AD-26 and AD-28 repeat R-10 almost word for word, but they state the design stance (no access-control layer, local processing), so they were not counted.

labels.note: Every tested label points to a test that asserts the behaviour. The weakest, R-2 'tested' through the e2e 'MADR ADR was not created by init' assertion, holds indirectly: init creates the MADR ADR only when adr list --raw prints nothing in an empty project, so the assertion requires empty raw output with no header. Guesses are marked 'Inferred, not verified' (R-1 b9-b10, R-9 b8, R-10 b1, R-10 b4), and the AD Why lines use stated or inferred correctly.

summary: Reliable: the listing path is described precisely and correctly: options, table and raw formats, the status filter and its errors, ordering, slug identity, every DTO field (including that there is no id or date field and that three dates exist), config discovery, error and exit handling including the launcher that drops the exit status, and all 19 tracked decision records mapped one-to-one with both supersessions and the fixtures excluded; all 15 sampled bullets and 32 of 33 decisions match the code, with no label errors. Wrong: only AD-21 has a wrong detail (init's registration has no known-error wrapper, so the command shape it describes holds for list and new only); minor leakage: 5 spec bullets name internals (the core, the web package, the debug helper, the command wrapper, Next.js), and AD-22 and AD-29 restate output behaviour. Missing: nothing from EXPECTED (7/7), and the ground truth is itself wrong on L7's counts (the repo has 11 records in docs/adr and 5 in packages/web/docs/adr, 19 in all, as the baseline says); the baseline did not notice that execWithErrorHandler throws its FailureExit on a detached promise (the template error is printed twice) and R-6 b6 leaves out that the author is also 'Anonymous' when Git has no user.name.
